title: WAL Replay Restore
description: Replays the write-ahead log from a base backup forward to the target timestamp, reconstructing the exact database state at that moment. Because every change is logged before it is applied, replay is deterministic: the same log always rebuilds the same state.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Base Backup plus WAL
description: Combines a periodic full base backup with continuous WAL archiving, so recovery needs only the latest base plus the log tail. This is the workhorse of point-in-time recovery: base backups bound how much log must replay, keeping restores fast even for old targets.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Snapshot Chains
description: Takes copy-on-write snapshots that freeze the storage state instantly, then chains incremental snapshots that record only changed blocks. Any snapshot in the chain can be mounted directly, giving near-instant recovery to many past moments without replaying logs.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Log Shipping to Standby
description: Streams WAL segments to a standby server as they are written, keeping a warm replica seconds behind the primary. On primary failure the standby replays the final segments and promotes, giving both disaster recovery and a ready source for point-in-time queries.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Point-in-Time Target Selection
description: Lets operators pick any timestamp - or a named restore point like 'before the migration' - and rebuilds exactly that state. Named restore points are cheap markers in the log, so teams can label risky operations and roll back to just before them with one command.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Backup Verification Restores
description: Automatically restores a sample of backups into an isolated environment and runs sanity checks, proving the backups actually work. Unverified backups are just hope; scheduled verification turns them into evidence that recovery will succeed when it matters.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Immutable Backup Copies
description: Stores backup copies in write-once object-locked storage that even administrators cannot delete or alter until retention expires. Ransomware that encrypts the primary and the regular backups still cannot touch the immutable copies, preserving a clean restore path.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: RPO and RTO Planning
description: Defines the recovery point objective (how much data loss is tolerable) and recovery time objective (how long downtime may last), then engineers the backup strategy to meet both. These two numbers turn vague 'back things up' into measurable targets the whole team can design and test against.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Table-Level Restore
description: Recovers a single table from backup without restoring the entire database, which is far faster when one table is damaged or was accidentally truncated. The restore extracts just the needed pages and replays only their log records.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Cross-Region Replicas
description: Maintains live replicas in distant regions so a regional outage or disaster cannot take the data with it. Asynchronous shipping keeps latency low while still bounding data loss to seconds, and each region can serve point-in-time reads locally.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Continuous Archiving
description: Archives every WAL segment to durable storage the moment it fills, creating an unbroken history from the first backup onward. With continuous archiving, any moment since archiving began is recoverable - the archive is the database's complete memory.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Retention Policies
description: Defines how long each backup tier is kept - hourly for a day, daily for a month, monthly for years - balancing recoverability against storage cost. Automated enforcement prunes expired backups so storage stays bounded without manual cleanup.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Corruption Detection Checksums
description: Checksums every backup block at write time and re-verifies on read, catching bit rot and transfer corruption before a restore depends on the data. A backup that fails verification is flagged and replaced from a healthy copy automatically.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Disaster Runbooks
description: Documents the exact recovery steps - who does what, in which order, with which commands - so a 3 AM outage does not depend on anyone's memory. Runbooks are tested in game days and updated after every real incident, keeping them honest.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.

title: Automated Restore Drills
description: Schedules full recovery rehearsals that spin up isolated copies and walk the runbook end to end without human prompting. Regular drills expose broken backups, stale credentials, and outdated steps while everything is still calm and fixable.
provenance: Public technical knowledge compiled from standard references and documentation; verified 2026-10-21.
